biological.citation: HDAC2 promotes autophagy-associated HCC malignant progression by transcriptionally activating LAPTM4B (PMID: 39147759)
biological.summary: HDAC2 expression is elevated in HCC tissues and is an independent predictor of poor prognosis. HDAC2 binds to four distinct sites on the LAPTM4B promoter to transcriptionally activate it, thereby promoting autophagy and malignant progression in HCC. Selective HDAC2 inhibition alleviated malignant HCC development in vitro and in vivo.

Using genetically defined models, HDAC2 was shown to be a cellular fitness factor controlling cell cycle in vitro and metastasis in vivo, particularly in undifferentiated mesenchymal PDAC cells. HDAC2 maintained expression of prosurvival receptor tyrosine kinases (PDGFRα, PDGFRβ, EGFR) and disabled the tumor-suppressive arm of the TGFβ pathway. HDAC2-deficient PDAC cells showed impaired metastasis formation.

biological.citation: Neuronal susceptibility to beta-amyloid toxicity and ischemic injury involves histone deacetylase-2 regulation of endophilin-B1 (PMID: 30028551)
biological.summary: HDAC2 is highly expressed in adult brain and its levels are elevated in Alzheimer's disease brain. HDAC2 suppresses neuron-specific Endophilin-B1 (Endo-B1) expression; HDAC2 knockdown or knockout enhances Endo-B1 expression while overexpression decreases it. HDAC2 knockout mice showed reduced injury in a cerebral ischemia model, with enhanced neuronal survival and normalized mitochondrial dynamics genes.

biological.citation: YTHDC1 is downregulated by the YY1/HDAC2 complex and controls the sensitivity of ccRCC to sunitinib by targeting the ANXA1-MAPK pathway (PMID: 35974388)
biological.summary: HDAC2 forms a complex with the transcription factor YY1 to transcriptionally repress YTHDC1 in clear cell renal cell carcinoma. This YY1/HDAC2/YTHDC1/ANXA1 axis modulates ccRCC progression and chemosensitivity to sunitinib. HDAC2 inhibitors were shown to resensitize ccRCC cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

biological.citation: HRD1-mediated ubiquitination of HDAC2 regulates PPARα-mediated autophagy and alleviates metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (PMID: 38815686)
biological.summary: HDAC2 acts as a transcriptional repressor of PPARα by binding to its promoter, thereby suppressing autophagy in hepatocytes under hypoxic conditions. The E3 ubiquitin ligase HRD1 mediates proteasomal degradation of HDAC2, relieving PPARα repression and restoring autophagy. This HRD1/HDAC2/PPARα axis was validated in a hypoxia-induced MAFLD mouse model.

biological.citation: PIM1-HDAC2 axis modulates intestinal homeostasis through epigenetic modification (PMID: 39027246)
biological.summary: PIM1 kinase physically interacts with HDAC2 and downregulates its protein level via phosphorylation in colonic epithelial cells. This PIM1-mediated reduction of HDAC2 alters epigenetic profiles of Wnt signaling pathway genes, impairing goblet cell differentiation and promoting susceptibility to colitis and colitis-associated colorectal cancer. The findings were validated in ulcerative colitis patient samples and murine models.

biological.citation: CoREST3 exhibits isoform specific expression in Alzheimer's disease and regulation of HDAC2 (PMID: 40817058)
biological.summary: HDAC2 protein levels were significantly decreased by >50% in the superior temporal gyrus, precuneus, and primary visual cortex of Alzheimer's disease post mortem brain tissue. CoREST3 binds upstream of the HDAC2 transcription start site in iPSC-derived cortical neurons and regulates HDAC2 in an isoform-specific manner: CoREST3 isoform A overexpression increased HDAC2 protein twofold, while isoform F reduced it by 48%. Dysregulated CoREST3 expression in AD may contribute to altered HDAC2 levels involved in AD pathogenesis.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Large-scale trans-ethnic genome-wide association study reveals novel loci, causal molecular mechanisms and effector genes for kidney function (A.P. Morris et al.)
biological.summary: Integration of eGFR GWAS signals with functional and regulatory annotation revealed that association signals were jointly enriched in binding sites for HDAC2 and EZH2 in kidney tissue. Class I histone deacetylases including HDAC2 are noted to be required for embryonic kidney gene expression, growth, and differentiation. This implicates HDAC2 binding sites as regulatory elements underlying genetic associations with kidney function.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Systematic analysis of nonsense-mediated decay escaping protein-truncating variants in 97,728 clinical exomes identifies new Mendelian disease genes (R. Torene et al.)
biological.summary: Nine cases with syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD) carried protein-truncating variants that escape nonsense-mediated decay (PTVesc) de novo mutations in HDAC2, identifying it as a candidate NDD disease gene. HDAC2 is a histone modifier, a known mechanism of NDD pathogenesis, and was identified through systematic analysis of de novo mutations in clinical exomes. The finding suggests PTVesc in HDAC2 may act as a hypomorph, antimorph, or neomorph mechanism.

biological.citation: ASHG 2012 - Expression patterns of histone acetylation modifier genes in gastric cancer (F. Wisnieski et al.)
biological.summary: HDAC2 mRNA expression was significantly higher in primary gastric adenocarcinoma tumor tissue compared to adjacent non-tumor tissue by RT-qPCR. HDAC2 expression was also higher in intestinal-type than diffuse-type gastric cancer. These findings suggest HDAC2 may serve as a biomarker for gastric cancer diagnosis or a target for gene therapy.
biological.sample_size: 38 matched gastric tumor and non-tumor tissue pairs
